newsitem.title: ALBANIA: Hundreds of Albanian investors clash with police.
newsitem.headline: Hundreds of Albanian investors clash with police.

text.p: Hundreds of angry protestors clashed with Albanian police on Wednesday as they demanded the return of their money from a get-rich-quick pyramid scheme, eyewitnesses said.

Some 500 demonstrators broke away from a crowd of 5,000 that had gathered outside the offices of Sude pyramid scheme in western Tirana. They marched the two kilometres (one mile) to the capital's main Skanderbeg Square, where they were met by police wielding batons.
"We want our money back. Sali Berisha you are a thief. Meksi you are a thief," the crowd chanted, directing much of its anger against President Berisha and Prime Minister Aleksander Meksi.

Pyramid schemes, offering returns of up to 200 percent over three months, have sprung up across the impoverished Balkan nation since the fall of communism. Sude ceased making repayments to depositors in November.
"Look what they have done to us," said an elderly man, bearing a wound he said was inflicted by a police baton. "But we have nothing to lose."
Frustrated by police blockades in their attempts to enter Skanderbeg Square, some 200 demonstrators chose instead to occupy a main road circling central Tirana, bringing traffic to a standstill.
